title: "Theory"

# Theory: Identity and Config are Data, Not Login

Git does not have accounts. It has **key-value config** and **author strings baked into commits**. A forge later *matches* those strings to a user.

## Invariants

1. Config is three layers: system (`/etc/gitconfig`), global (`~/.gitconfig`), local (`.git/config`). **Later overrides earlier.**
2. `user.name` and `user.email` are copied into every commit object. Changing config does not rewrite old commits.
3. Authentication to a **remote** (SSH key or HTTPS token) is separate from commit identity.
4. `init.defaultBranch` only affects **new** repositories.

```text
  /etc/gitconfig          machine
  ~/.gitconfig            you
  .git/config             this repo     ← wins

  user.email ──► commit.author     (history)
  SSH key    ──► git@host          (transport)
```

## Why layers

One person, two emails (home and work) is a local or `includeIf` problem, not a second Git install. One laptop, several forges, is several keys in `~/.ssh/config`, not several `user.name`s.

## What can break

- Commits with `$USER@$HOSTNAME` because identity was never set (`user.useConfigOnly` refuses that).
- Pushing with HTTPS using an account password; most forges want a **token**.
- Setting `core.autocrlf` on Linux and fighting LF files.
- Assuming `core.editor` is optional and then hanging in `vim` on `git commit` with no `-m`.

## How to read this chapter

Install is PATH and version. Layers are which file won (`--show-origin`). Identity is what history will say. SSH vs HTTPS is how a remote will know you. Editor, aliases, and updates are the Linux daily driver.
